newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour reaffirms commitment to Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour reaffirms commitment to Eurofighter.

text.p: Britain's pre-election skirmishing spread to defence on Friday as the ruling Conservatives and the main opposition Labour party clashed over the future of the Eurofighter project.
Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said Labour's pledge to conduct a wholesale review of Britain's defence budget if it wins power meant spending cuts were inevitable.
"I am sure that review will lead to cuts," Portillo said in a speech in Lancashire, northwest England. "The instinct of Labour governments is to cut defence."

Portillo said Eurofighter's price tag of 40 million pounds ($64 million) per plane would make the project an obvious target for Labour's cost-conscious Gordon Brown, who would be finance minister if the party wins the coming election.
But Labour's defence spokesman, David Clark, said Labour had consistently backed Eurofighter, which he said was vital to Britain's future defence needs.
"It is grossly irresponsible of Michael Portillo to create uncertainty over the future of the Eurofighter project by spreading lies about Labour's plans," Clark said in a statement.
"Discussions with our German partners are at a delicate stage, and Mr Portillo's wilful scaremongering threatens to do irreparable damage to the British defence industry," he added.

Eurofighter is being built by an industrial consortium made up of Daimler-Benz Aerosapce AG, British Aerospace Plc Italy's Alenia and CASA of Spain, which hope their governments will havea memoranddum of understanding on the jet fighter project by the end of 1997. ($1=.6237 Pound)
